test_title: PYST 44: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Under which Act was the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), which conducts Lok Adalats along with other Legal Services Institutions, constituted?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** was constituted under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**.
 
• The primary aim of NALSA is to ensure **free legal aid** to weaker sections of society and promote justice on the basis of equal opportunity.
 
• It works to organize **Lok Adalats**, which are informal courts that resolve disputes through conciliation and settlement.
 
• The Act emphasizes providing **legal services** to marginalized groups such as women, children, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other vulnerable communities.
 
• Under this Act, **State Legal Services Authorities** were also created to implement policies and organize legal aid programs at the state level.
 
• It is an important law for ensuring compliance with **Article 39A** of the Indian Constitution, which mandates free legal aid to economically weaker sections and promotes equality before the law.
 
• The Act also empowers NALSA to conduct **legal awareness campaigns** to educate citizens about their rights and duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Public Interest Litigation Act, 1990**__

 __
 
• There is no specific law called the **Public Interest Litigation Act, 1990**. Public Interest Litigation (PIL) refers to a judicial process under which cases can be filed for protecting public interests.
 
• PILs are governed by various provisions of the **Indian Constitution**, especially **Articles 32 and 226**, which allow individuals to approach the Supreme Court or High Courts.
 
• This concept was introduced in the 1980s and is not linked to a specific act but rather to judicial activism.
 
 
 
• **Advocates Act, 1961**__
 __
 
• The **Advocates Act, 1961** governs the legal profession in India and provides for the establishment of the **Bar Council of India** and State Bar Councils.
 
• It regulates the standards of professional conduct, etiquette, and legal education for advocates.
 
• This Act focuses on the administration and organization of the legal profession rather than providing legal aid services.
 
 
 
• **Indian Bar Council Act, 1926**__
 
 
• The **Indian Bar Council Act, 1926** was enacted to provide for the establishment of Bar Councils in different provinces and regulate the legal profession.
 
• It was a precursor to the **Advocates Act, 1961** and laid the foundation for the legal profession in India.
 
• This Act does not deal with legal aid or the organization of Lok Adalats.
